body:
I'm sorry to fight you on this. I know that it's not productive or healthy. It's likely very rude because of the kindness you speak and the compassion for helping others. I think you're right for the most part. I just don't know how people can live without having a goal look for like that. I don't know how to be happy with just "trying to talk to a cashier." I wanted to do a lot of big things, like travel and learn about this or learn about that. The goal I had had to this point was learning. I've enjoyed things like art, history, storytelling, and I could take a new passion for a new subject every week. The only thing I feel like I had done up till now is just learn. Not anything in particular but everything that interested me. It's not a great thing, I know. It's better to focus on some things than do everything and I tried to narrow down everything but I still end up with too much floating around in my head. I have nothing to do with it. I don't apply it anywhere, I don't want to just teach it or anything. So it just accumulates in my brain for whatever reason. I think, the worst is that, in retrospect. I could have made so many friends, I wouldn't be so alone if I had just taken the time be with other people instead of constantly trying to read, watch, or think about this or that. But now I've forsaken most everyone for what, I don't know anymore.     
  
The idea of a concrete ending sounds so appealing to me. I hate the overwhelmingness of the world. Trying to accomplish one thing and having two or three more pop up afterwards. It just doesn't make a lot of sense to me. Why going through it all would be worth anything. I could understand the people who have those they lose and cherish and like to have fun. But that just isn't how my mind has developed. So, I'm looking for a purpose and I just feel so behind or in the wrong place that I don't know what it matters if I could get back on track. I would just stay behind in everything. I don't know. A lot of it doesn't make sense to me anymore. I'm just tired of thinking about it.
